title: Station 7, the circuit
note: Fictional patient. DRAFT pending clinical sign-off. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: Same arrest as Module 5: Mr. Arnel Gutierrez, 61, forearm fistula, 2.1 L removed of a 3.2 L goal. Compressions have started. You are his assigned nurse, now the circuit nurse. A saline bag dripped earlier and the chair is wet near his arm.

choices.text: Stop fluid removal and say it aloud.
choices.feedback: Fluid removal empties a circulation that has none to spare.
The circuit needs one owner; leaving it unmanaged keeps removing fluid.
choices.then: The leader sends you back to the machine.

n2.scene: No air, no abnormal blood color, lines intact, no reaction signs.

choices.text: Return the blood quickly with saline (or clamp and disconnect if that would take you away from something more urgent), and announce it.
choices.feedback: With no circuit cause, return the blood volume (ERC) or clamp and disconnect (Card 1).

choices.text: Leave the pump running and keep dialyzing during CPR.
choices.feedback: A running circuit during arrest is unmanaged and may keep removing volume.
choices.then: The leader asks you to stop and return.

choices.text: Spend four minutes on a full rinse-back program.
choices.feedback: The decision should take seconds; a long rinse-back pulls you from the team.

n3.prompt: What must be true before the shock?

choices.text: Wet drapes wiped or moved, pads on dry skin away from the fistula arm, the machine disconnected unless rated defibrillation-proof, your hands off the lines at “clear.”
choices.feedback: ERC: disconnect unless defibrillation-proof, beware wet surfaces.

choices.text: Hold the lines steady during the shock so the needles do not move.
choices.feedback: The lines touch the patient and can carry current to you.
choices.then: You let go when the leader repeats “clear.”

choices.text: The secured venous needle with a saline-primed line, flush before and after; tell the leader it is ready.
choices.feedback: ERC: leave the access open (working, secured) and use it for drugs.

choices.text: Start a new IV in the fistula arm.
choices.feedback: Avoid the fistula arm; the existing venous needle is ready and safer.

end.title: 10:05 a.m.
end.text: Handover: two hours on the machine, 2.1 L removed, blood returned at the start, last potassium, fistula needles secured. Dialysis is not restarted without the attending nephrologist.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Stop fluid removal first.
  • Decide and announce the blood: return or clamp; never return after air, hemolysis or reaction.
  • Before the shock: dry, pads clear, disconnected unless rated, hands off.
  • Use the access safely for drugs.
